subject: Basic Science
title: Fiji Year 10 Mock Examination — Basic Science
instructions:
Answer ALL questions. Time allowed: 2 hours (an extra 10 minutes is allowed for reading).
Multiple-choice: click the letter of the best answer (click again to clear).
Short answers and paragraphs: type your answer in English in the box. Show working for calculations.
You may use a calculator. Round answers to 2 decimal places unless stated otherwise.
Your answers are saved automatically. The paper is submitted automatically when time runs out.
Strand 1 has one essay question with two options — write ONE essay (about 150–250 words) with an introduction, body and conclusion.
Diagrams are described in words.

questions.text:
13. Human digestive system
(i) Name the organ where most digestion and absorption of food take place. (1 mark)
(ii) Explain the role of the liver in digestion. (2 marks)
(iii) Explain one difference between the roles of the stomach and the large intestine. (2 marks)
questions.model:
(i) Small intestine (1)
(ii) The liver produces bile (1), which breaks fats into small droplets (emulsifies) so that enzymes can digest them faster (1).
(iii) Stomach: churns food and digests protein using pepsin and acid (1); large intestine: absorbs water from undigested food and forms faeces (1).

questions.text: 14. Write the word equation for aerobic respiration.
questions.model: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water (+ energy). Reactants correct (1), products correct (1).

questions.text:
15. A food web in a forest is described below:
grass → grasshopper → frog → snake
grass → rat → snake
rat → owl
grasshopper → bird → owl

(i) Define the term herbivore. (1 mark)
(ii) Identify the producer. (1 mark)
(iii) Identify one secondary consumer. (1 mark)
(iv) Suggest what would happen to the number of frogs if all the snakes were removed. Give a reason. (1 mark)
questions.model:
(i) An animal that eats only plants (1)
(ii) Grass (1)
(iii) Frog or bird (also accept snake or owl, which are secondary consumers when they eat the rat) (1)
(iv) Frogs would increase because their predator is gone (1)

questions.text: 16. Define phototropism.
questions.model: The growth response of a plant (shoot) towards or away from light (1).

questions.text:
17. Coral reefs
(i) State two reasons why coral reefs are important to Fiji. (2 marks)
(ii) Explain one human activity that threatens coral reefs. (2 marks)
(iii) State two ways people can protect coral reefs. (2 marks)
questions.model:
(i) Any two: home/breeding ground for fish; food and income for communities; protect coast from waves; tourism (2)
(ii) e.g. Dynamite fishing / pollution / sediment from logging / coral mining / anchoring (1) — breaks or smothers corals so they die (1).
(iii) Any two: marine protected areas / tabu areas; no dynamite or poison fishing; reduce pollution and littering; avoid standing on corals; reduce sediment by replanting (2)

questions.text:
18. ESSAY QUESTION (10 marks)
Write ONE essay on either Option 1 or Option 2. Marks: Introduction 1, Content 8, Conclusion 1.
questions.model:
Option 1: (i) Digestion = breakdown of large insoluble food into small soluble molecules that can be absorbed (1); balanced diet = food with all nutrients in the right amounts (1). (ii) Any two organs, 2 each: mouth – chewing (mechanical) and amylase on starch; stomach – churning, pepsin and HCl on protein; small intestine – completes digestion, absorbs via villi; large intestine – absorbs water. (iii) Any two food tests: iodine → blue-black for starch; Benedict's + heat → brick-red for glucose; biuret → purple for protein; paper/ethanol test for fats (2).
Option 2: (i) Ecosystem = a community of organisms interacting with each other and their non-living environment (1); mangrove = salt-tolerant trees growing in the intertidal zone (1). (ii) Any two, 2 each: nursery/breeding ground for fish and crabs; protects coast from erosion and storm surges; traps sediment and filters pollutants; source of firewood, food, medicine. (iii) Any two: replant mangroves; laws/permits against clearing; community awareness programmes; reduce rubbish dumping (2).
Introduction (1) and conclusion (1) must be relevant.

choices.text:
Option 1 — Sub-strand: Nutrition and Digestion
The food we eat must be digested before the body can use it.
In your essay:
(i) Define digestion and balanced diet; (2 marks)
(ii) Describe the role of two organs in the digestive system; (4 marks)
(iii) Describe two food tests used in the laboratory. (2 marks)

Option 2 — Sub-strand: Biodiversity, Change and Sustainability
Mangroves are among the most important ecosystems in Fiji.
In your essay:
(i) Define the terms ecosystem and mangrove; (2 marks)
(ii) Describe two reasons why mangroves are important; (4 marks)
(iii) State two ways mangroves can be conserved. (2 marks)

7. Sodium has a mass number of 23 and an atomic number of 11.
(i) How many protons does a sodium atom have? (1 mark)
(ii) Calculate the number of neutrons. Show your working. (2 marks)
(iii) Write the electron arrangement of sodium. (1 mark)
questions.model:
(i) 11 (1)
(ii) neutrons = mass number − atomic number (1) = 23 − 11 = 12 (1)
(iii) 2, 8, 1 (1)

questions.text: 8. Explain one difference between a physical change and a chemical change.
questions.model: A physical change makes no new substance and is usually reversible, e.g. melting ice (1); a chemical change forms a new substance and is hard to reverse, e.g. burning paper (1).

questions.text: 9. A piece of magnesium ribbon is held in a flame. Give two observations.
questions.model: Burns with a very bright white light/flame (1); a white powder (magnesium oxide) is left (1).

questions.text: 10. Describe the process of annealing a metal and state its purpose.
questions.model: Heat the metal until red hot and then let it cool slowly (1); this makes the metal softer and less brittle / easier to work (1).

questions.text:
11. Balance the equation by writing the missing numbers:
__ Mg + O₂ → __ MgO
questions.model: 2 Mg + O₂ → 2 MgO (1 mark each number)

questions.text: 12. Students added the same mass of marble chips (test-tube A) and powdered marble (test-tube B) to the same acid. The reaction in B was faster. Explain why.
questions.model: Powder has a larger surface area (1), so more particles are exposed and there are more collisions with the acid per second (1).

9. White light passes through a triangular prism and splits into colours.
Name this process and list the seven colours in order.
questions.model: Dispersion (1); red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet (1)

questions.text: 10. State one way of caring for lenses (e.g. spectacles or a microscope).
questions.model: Clean with lens paper/soft cloth / keep in a case / do not touch with fingers / avoid scratching (1)

questions.text: 11. Describe what happens to a parallel beam of light when it passes through a convex lens.
questions.model: The rays are refracted (bent) inwards / converge (1) and meet at one point called the principal focus (1).

questions.text: 12. State two renewable energy sources used in Fiji.
questions.model: Any two: hydro (e.g. Monasavu), solar, wind (e.g. Butoni), biomass/bagasse, geothermal (2)

questions.text:
13. A bicycle dynamo (generator) lights a lamp when the wheel turns.
(i) State the energy change in the dynamo. (1 mark)
(ii) State one way to increase the current produced. (1 mark)
questions.model:
(i) Kinetic/mechanical energy → electrical energy (1)
(ii) Turn faster / stronger magnet / more turns of wire in the coil (1)

questions.text:
14. Electrical wiring in houses uses parallel circuits.
(i) Explain one difference between a series and a parallel circuit. (1 mark)
(ii) State one advantage of a parallel circuit. (1 mark)
questions.model:
(i) Series has one path for current; parallel has more than one path / branches (1)
(ii) If one bulb blows the others stay on / each can be switched separately / full voltage to each (1)

questions.text:
15. A 2 000 W kettle is used for 30 minutes every day for 7 days. Electricity costs 40 cents per unit (1 unit = 1 kWh).
(i) Calculate the units used in one week. (2 marks)
(ii) Calculate the cost for the week. (1 mark)

16. A car speeds up from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 4 s.
(i) Calculate the change in velocity. (1 mark)
(ii) Calculate the acceleration. (2 marks)
questions.model:
(i) 30 − 10 = 20 m/s (1)
(ii) a = change in velocity ÷ time = 20 ÷ 4 (1) = 5 m/s² (1)

5. State two features of the Earth that allow it to support life.
questions.model: Any two: liquid water; oxygen in the atmosphere; suitable temperature / right distance from the Sun; ozone layer; atmosphere that keeps heat (2)

questions.text: 6. Define the greenhouse effect.
questions.model: Gases in the atmosphere (CO₂, water vapour, methane) trap heat radiated from the Earth's surface (1), keeping the Earth warm enough for life (1).

questions.text: 7. Name one ozone-depleting substance and state one effect of ozone depletion on human health.
questions.model: CFCs (chlorofluorocarbons) / halons (1); skin cancer / sunburn / eye cataracts (1)

questions.text: 8. State two effects of sea-level rise on coastal communities in Fiji.
questions.model: Any two: coastal erosion; flooding of homes; salt water entering wells and gardens; villages forced to relocate; loss of land (2)

questions.text: 9. Describe one way a community can show resilience to the impacts of climate change.
questions.model: e.g. Relocating the village to higher ground / building sea walls and planting mangroves (1), which reduces damage from storm surges and flooding (1).

questions.text: 10. Explain the difference between weather and climate.
questions.model: Weather is the day-to-day condition of the atmosphere; climate is the average weather of a place over a long period (about 30 years) (1).
